svg.title: One level at a time vs one token at a time
svg.desc: Split screen with a shared model-call counter and the same 128-token TinyStories text in both panels. Left, the NCM writes all 128 positions from the first level and sharpens them level by level, done after 11 calls; its first level reads: Once upon a time, there was a little named.. The. a.... the.. the.. the. the play. the… Right, the autoregressive model replays the same tokens one per call (forced decoding, not an independent sample) and needs 128 calls; after 11 calls it has: Then, on a time, in a big forest, Both end with: Then, on a time, in a big forest, there was a little bunny named Kiki. Kiki loved to play and all day long. She liked to…

Real NCM output of an independently trained 87M MLX NCM: unconditional TinyStories sample 0 of 16, seed 0, temperature 1, shown in
full: all 128 tokens of the window.
AR panel: our 91M autoregressive baseline (same blocks, same training windows) replays the same 128 tokens one call per token (forced
decoding) to compare model calls for identical output; it is not an independent AR sample.
Model calls are counted, not timed: an NCM call is larger than an AR call, and NCM adds a codec decode. NCM level 1 of 12 is drawn from
a stored unigram without a call, so its 12 levels take 11 calls. Bold marks tokens changed by the latest NCM level.
Whitespace is collapsed to single spaces in both panels. The first NCM sample of the seed with a well-formed first sentence. SHA-256
